## WHAT: Defining a population is multi-faceted
<hr>

* **A group of organisms from one species can be evaluated in many ways**
    + abundance
    + sex ratios
    + age structure
    + density
    
<br/>

* **Defining the population boundary is tricky**
    + a lake
    + a lake and incoming streams
    + the whole watershed 

<br/>

* **Aphid population: leaf, plant, grassland, ecosystem?**
    + depends on the study and the question

## WHO: Definition of an individual can be tricky
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">
* **Unitary organism: forming a single entity**
    + deer, bird, spider, human, etc.

<br/>

* **Modular organisms: colonies**
    + bacteria, algae, corals, biofilms
    + certain plants: ferns grow by rhizomes

<br/>

* **Some modular organisms may themselves be ecological populations**
    + One coral colony contains many connected polyps, and each polyp grows, feeds, reproduces, and dies
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:575px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/hayscentedfern.jpg">

## Life history trait examples: Dormancy
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 100%;">

* **Some organisms spend part of their life cycle dormant**
    + seeds, spores, resting eggs, developmental arrest, etc.

<br/>

</div>

* **Dormant individuals can be a large, hidden part of a population**
    + thousands of viable seeds may occur in a square meter of soil
    
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

* **Allows individuals to survive unfavorable conditions**
    + some remain dormant for very long times

<br/>

* **How does this complicate population dynamics?**  
    + dormant individuals are easy to miss when estimating population size
    + offspring produce may not enter the next active generation
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:370px; LEFT:605px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/seeds.jpg">

## Life history traits: Reproductive conflict
<hr>
<br/>

* **Goal to pass on genes...**

<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

* **When and how to spend your resources**
    + <span style="color:red">reproduction comes at a cost of growth</span>
    + ↑ flowers + seeds = ↓ leaves and roots
    + are enough resources available to support pregnancy in animals?
    + *surviving vs growing the population is the conflict*
<br/>

* **Life histories of males and females may differ due to reproductive investment**

## Survival and reproduction determine population change
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

* **Birth rates and survivorship tell us whether a population is likely to grow, shrink, or remain stable**

<br/>

* **Survival and reproduction differ among ages or life stages**
    + juveniles, reproductive adults, and older individuals contribute differently to population growth

<br/>

* **Life tables summarize these age-specific patterns**
    + *Cohort*: follow individuals born at the same time through their lives
    + *Static*: compare the ages of individuals present at one point in time

<br/>

* **These patterns reveal more than population size alone**
    + age structure, when mortality is high, which age contributes the most to population growth, etc.
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:635px; WIDTH:425px; HEIGHT:425px" SRC="images/life_table1.png">

## r/K selection theory: Growth and reproduction strategies
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

* **r-selected species: “cheap” offspring**

<br/>

* **K-selected species: “expensive” offspring**

<br/>
<br/>

* **These are the 2 ends of a spectrum**

## Populations with unlimited resources: **Exponential growth**
<hr>
**Population growth that accelerates because a larger population produces more new individuals at constant rates**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:50px; WIDTH:650px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/elephant2.jpg">

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:750px; WIDTH:300px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/kruger2.png">

## Population growth eventually faces environmental resistance
<hr>
<br/>

* **Density-dependent**
    + competition
    + predation
    + disease
    + resources
 
<br/>

* **Density-independent**
    + catastrophic events
    + disturbances

<br/>

* **Carrying Capacity: maximum size of a population an environment can support**
    + environmental resistance leads to **Logistic growth (S-shaped curve)**
    
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:375px; WIDTH:700px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/seals.png">

## Testable concepts in this lecture
<hr>

* **Population structure and measurement**
    + abundance, density, demographics, and population boundaries
    
<br/>

* **Population change**
    + births, deaths, immigration, emigration, and demographic structure
    
<br/>

* **Life history and survivorship**
    + reproductive strategies, dormancy, survivorship curves, and r/K selection
    
<br/>

* **Population growth and environmental limits**
    + exponential vs. logistic growth, environmental resistance, and carrying capacity
